Let \(q=p\), and fix once and for all a nonsquare \(\delta\in \mathbb F_p^\times\).

For a field \(E\subset M_8(\mathbb F_p)\) of order \(p^2\), the underlying \(8\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-space is a \(4\)-dimensional vector space over \(E\). Hence for \(x\in E\), its matrix trace is
\[
4\operatorname{Tr}_{E/\mathbb F_p}(x).
\]
Since \(p\) is odd, the trace-zero elements of \(E\) form a \(1\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-line. If \(0\ne A\) lies on that line, then \(A^2\in \mathbb F_p^\times I\), and \(A^2\) is a nonsquare scalar multiple of \(I\). Thus each admissible field \(E\) corresponds to a line
\[
\mathbb F_p A,\qquad A^T=-A,\qquad A^2=\lambda I
\]
with \(\lambda\) nonsquare.

After scaling \(A\), every such line has exactly two representatives satisfying
\[
A^T=-A,\qquad A^2=\delta I.
\]
Therefore an ordered sextuple of fields is counted by ordered sextuples
\[
(A_1,\dots,A_6)
\]
with
\[
A_i^T=-A_i,\qquad A_i^2=\delta I,\qquad A_iA_j=-A_jA_i\quad(i\ne j),
\]
divided by \(2^6\).

Now the matrices \(A_1,\dots,A_6\) give a representation of the Clifford algebra on generators \(e_i\) satisfying
\[
e_i^2=\delta,\qquad e_ie_j=-e_je_i.
\]
This Clifford algebra has dimension \(2^6=64\), is central simple over \(\mathbb F_p\), and over a finite field it is split, so it is isomorphic to \(M_8(\mathbb F_p)\). Its involution \(e_i\mapsto -e_i\) corresponds to transpose. Hence admissible normalized sextuples are exactly the images of a fixed Clifford generating sextuple under automorphisms of \((M_8(\mathbb F_p),T)\).

The automorphism group of \(M_8(\mathbb F_p)\) preserving transpose is the projective orthogonal similitude group
\[
\operatorname{PGO}_8^+(\mathbb F_p).
\]
For the split \(8\)-dimensional quadratic form,
\[
|\operatorname{PGO}_8^+(\mathbb F_p)|=|O_8^+(\mathbb F_p)|.
\]
The order of the split orthogonal group is
\[
|O_8^+(\mathbb F_p)|
=
2p^{12}(p^4-1)(p^2-1)(p^4-1)(p^6-1).
\]
Thus the number of normalized sextuples is
\[
2p^{12}(p^2-1)(p^4-1)^2(p^6-1).
\]
Dividing by \(2^6\), since each field has exactly two normalized trace-zero generators, gives
\[
\frac{2p^{12}(p^2-1)(p^4-1)^2(p^6-1)}{64}
=
\frac{p^{12}(p^2-1)(p^4-1)^2(p^6-1)}{32}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{p^{12}(p^2-1)(p^4-1)^2(p^6-1)}{32}}
\]
